title: Effects of altering levothyroxine (L-T4) doses on quality of life, mood, and cognition in L-T4 treated subjects
authors: Samuels MH, Kolobova I, Niederhausen M, Janowsky JS, Schuff KG
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: Adults with levothyroxine-treated hypothyroidism and normal TSH at Oregon Health and Science University
funder: This work was supported by National Institutes of Health Grants R01 DK075496 (to M.H.S.) and UL1 RR024120 (to OHSU).
authorConflicts: The authors have nothing to disclose.
result: Doses were adjusted double-blind to TSH targets of 0.34 to 2.50, 2.51 to 5.60 or 5.61 to 12.0 mU/l; final mean doses were 1.50, 1.32 and 0.78 µg/kg and mean TSH 1.85, 3.93 and 9.49 mU/l. Quality of life, mood, memory and executive function did not differ after correction for multiple comparisons. Participants could not tell how their dose had changed (P = 0.55), yet preferred the dose they perceived as higher (P < 0.001): 68% preferred the final dose when they thought it had risen and 96% the initial dose when they thought it had fallen.
